forecasts.reason: Math-identical recipe, so time and accuracy stay at the tip's; with cudnn.benchmark on and no deterministic flags, within-build nondeterminism (cuDNN wgrad) likely breaks arm (1), so pinning kernels can't give bit-identity.
Removes the 31x31 conv output, pool and their backward (~7-9% of a step), but a strided conv in place of conv+maxpool usually costs ~0.3-0.5 pp: ~1 s/pp, worse than the 1.5 s/pp H2.5 needs.
Net ~-5 steps plus the selection mechanism saves ~0.2 s; the accuracy delta of about -0.05 to -0.1 pp is below 3-seed resolution and probably below 20-seed resolution too.
13 more frozen steps at ~10 ms each save ~0.13 s, but the anneal window now starts at the 32 px switch and likely costs ~0.15 pp, so the cascade dose is near its cliff.

cruxes: How much held-out accuracy does the group-2 freeze plus top-up (I075) cost on same-build seeds 13-32? If it costs 0.05 pp or less, the cascade (I082) and its stacks are the best time lever left.
Is the seeds 0-2 spread caused by within-build nondeterminism or by kernel reselection at rebuild? This decides whether any sub-0.15 pp comparison can be resolved at all.
Does replacing conv1 + max-pool with a strided conv (I080) cost less than 0.25 pp? If so, removing the stem's full-resolution work is worth more than any remaining freeze dose.
structured_output.world_model: Tip E036: 5.31 s, population mean about 0.7525-0.7535. Time ≈ 0.25 s fixed + Σ steps × per-step cost. The average step is about 0.021 s; a frozen-group-2 step saves about 0.010 s. Backward truncation is still the cheapest lever, and its cost is set by the anneal window. Architecture cuts at the stem save time quickly but probably lose accuracy at about 1 s/pp. Boosters keep reading ≤0. Build-to-build noise is about ±0.25 pp on 3 seeds, probably partly from cuDNN nondeterminism.
